figure.head: Carlyle Photograph Albums, Album 7, Page 1
figure.caption: Photograph by Tait, "A Chelsea Interior," cropped to a square; above it a half-sheet of paper with lines in Thomas Carlyle's hand: "Whoso is hungry and list will eat, Let him come to Sprodborough to his meat; And for a night and for a day His horse shall have both corn and hay, And no men shall ask him when he goeth away. [Collins V 235.] " Inscription reads, "Brassplate on a Cross in the Highstreet of Sprodborough put up by a Fitzwilliam, pulled down, 1520. Near Doncaster."

figure.head: Carlyle Photograph Albums, Album 7, Page 7
figure.caption: Four photographs in ovals: of an older woman wearing a bonnet, inscribed "Margaret Aitken Carlyle" [Thomas Carlyle’s mother in the oft-copied portrait]; an unidentified man, seated with a book; Dr. "John Aitken Carlyle" in vignette and a portait of "Mrs. J.A. Carlyle", formerly Phoebe Elizabeth Hough Watt, in vignette. This is perhaps the only remaining image of J.A. Carlyle.
